title: Kind-segmented scope-aware address parser and resolver
description:
Replace the current two-segment qualified-id parser with a kind-segmented, scope-aware address parser and resolver, in jit's pure domain layer. Support three address forms: local-project items `@/<kind>/<self-id>`, issue items `@/issue/<short-id>/<kind>/<self-id>`, and a `<short-id>/<self-id>` sugar form that expands to the canonical issue form by inferring kind from id-pattern matching. A named-project segment (`@<name>` in place of the bare `@`) is recognized structurally as a scope token; declaring the project name and resolving named-project addresses are separate work outside this item. Resolution must match on the triple (scope, kind, self-id) rather than self-id alone, so items of different kinds sharing a scope no longer collide (for example a rule and a gate both named `coverage-preview`). The colon `:` stays reserved for the label `namespace:value` separator and never appears inside an address value.

This is foundational addressing-core work: jit's current qualified-id parser only splits a value on the first `/`, and its call sites compare the second segment by equality with no kind filter; per-scope self-id uniqueness is also enforced across all kinds sharing a scope with no kind dimension today. Both are barriers to introducing new addressable kinds without collision risk.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: local-project and issue-item address forms parse into scope, kind, and self-id components; a `@<name>` named-project segment parses structurally as a scope token, with its resolution against a declared project name outside this item.
- [hard] REQ-02: the sugar form expands to the canonical issue form by inferring kind from the id-pattern; ambiguous inference produces a clear error.
- [hard] REQ-03: resolution matches on (scope, kind, self-id); per-scope self-id uniqueness is rescoped to per-(scope, kind) so same-slug items of different kinds coexist.

Blast radius: the existing two-segment parser and its call sites across issue-show/resolve paths, validation, and blocking-graph analysis are replaced; per-scope self-id uniqueness enforcement gains the kind dimension, and any existing test asserting duplicate-self-id detection across kinds within one scope is updated to match. The resolver takes the configured kind list as a parameter, mirroring the existing kind-resolution function, so no kind name is hardcoded into engine code and the domain layer stays free of I/O.

## Amendment note (plan D3-A / D11-A, invoker-approved 2026-07-03)

REQ-02's ambiguity error holds at the pure-function level (`expand_sugar_address` returns `SugarKindAmbiguous`); at the resolution call sites, pattern-ambiguous sugar defers to the indexed items per plan amendment D3-A (single match resolves, genuine multi-item collision errors — never a silent first match), because the `requirement` kind's deliberately generic id-pattern makes every non-REQ sugar pattern-ambiguous. REQ-03's kind-filtered resolution holds for all explicit-kind addresses; the legacy kind-agnostic project form `@/<self-id>` remains resolvable as an explicitly-commented transitional path removed by story 7f22d6cf REQ-04 (amendment D11-A). Both amendments are recorded in the epic plan (dev/active/2821e177-2d2d-4b25-b64a-4f38723e7fe6-plan.md §Amendments).
